rows.text: My mission is the protection of the Underworld. The trust of the minority sample is redundant to my calculations.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Human behavior will always deviate from rational calculation, Clara...
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: As evidenced by their presence here.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Svarog! We haven't settled our final score.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Seele, subordinate to Wildfire... Your resistance is futile. The result of my calculation is unequivocal: Remaining in the Underworld is the optimal strategy for survival.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: *sigh* This again... Calculation results, survival strategies... I haven't got time for your thesis. Withdraw your forces, or I'll lose my temper!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Observe, Clara. Even under abject conditions, humans are unable to avoid division and conflict.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: But, Mr. Svarog...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Human failure to accept the calculation result is a significant threat to the survival strategy of the Underworld. Calculation complete, result unequivocal: Armed suppression of Wildfire and their allies is the optimal course of action.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: And more fashionably dressed, too... Hey, is he about to leave? What about the girl in red?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ah! What about the girl in red? That robot is gonna take her away!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We must leave, Clara. External variables have triggered a calculation reset. The Furnace Core hub requires protection.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: ...Please, Mills, don't hit them too hard.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: *sigh* I was getting bored of those minions — time for a real fight. Come at me!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Whew... not bad. How many of these big guys is Svarog hiding?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: A lot... which is why Wildfire has never been able to take him down. Svarog's forces are too strong. We don't have enough firepower.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Clara? Don't worry about her. That girl is best pals with Svarog — she's always following behind him. He wouldn't harm her.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Like I told you. That guy barely leaves his nest — it's rare to see him away from the Furnace Core. Even when he does appear, he doesn't stick around for long. He leaves everything to his subordinates.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: It might also have been because Clara was here — the little girl in red. She's best pals with Svarog — always following behind him.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I guess I'm just used to seeing them together now, even if I don't understand it. *sigh* Let's look for the chief.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: No need to look far.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Nice work, Seele. We were attacked on both sides by robots — who knows where they came from. We thought we were in it for the long haul, hahaha!
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Chief! Is everyone okay? Is anyone injured?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: We're fine — we're used to it at this point. We sent those pesky robots and ragtag troops packing. The mine should be quiet for a while.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: And who are your friends here...
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Ahh, them! They're outsiders that Sampo brought down from who-knows-where. They need a favor from Wildfire, so I brought them with me. It'll be faster if they explain.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Hahaha! That's quite the tone to take on our first meeting. I won't forget you in a hurry.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Hah, it's been a while since I heard that anyone was pleased to meet anyone, haha. I won't forget you in a hurry. Wildfire welcomes you.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: So, you went to all this trouble to find Wildfire. What help is it you need?
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Telling Oleg and Seele about what happened and your mission to look for the Stellaron...
Ha! I didn't know you'd put on a show for the Overworld too. Impressive.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Ho-ho, well this is new. Wildfire can barely take care of the Underworld, and now outsiders are looking for assistance from us.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: This "Stellaron" you speak of — I've never heard of it. But if it's a secret that even we locals don't know about, then one name does come to mind...
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Really? Sampo? You might as well try the supreme guardian.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: The current supreme guardian is a liar who uses sweet words to deceive the Underworld. She's never cared about our survival—
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Stop right there... I... won't allow you to insult the madam guardian.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Miss Overworld, my words may be painful to you, but every one of them is true. Go out into the towns and hear for yourself — see how the people here suffer.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: I haven't gotten close to voicing the extent of the Underworld's grievances, young lady. But I will respect your request. I will leave it at that, for now.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Let's get back to the main topic. The name that came to my mind, was Svarog.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Huh...!? Isn't Svarog Wildfire's sworn enemy?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Why would a mere robot in the Underworld have knowledge of important secrets?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Sworn enemy? Not how I see it. The young master here is closer. Svarog is a cold and unfeeling machine. He recognizes only the dead reasoning of his calculations.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Svarog is not against Wildfire... or perhaps I should say: Wildfire isn't even of concern to him. That ancient robot witnessed the war...
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: If you're looking to pick up a thread... he may well be your best source.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Don't judge a book by its cover. I myself have put a few centuries behind me. Would you be able to tell?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm familiar with over twenty {RUBY_B#Abominations of Abundance}long-life species{RUBY_E#} — none of them look like you.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hey! Would it kill you to play along?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah, I remember hearing this world was invaded by the Legion hundreds of years ago.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Robots don't forget. If Svarog hasn't heard of your Stellaron, then I'm afraid perhaps no one has.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: In which case, we need to think of a way to convince Svarog to communicate with us.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Or get him to hand over his memory bank. We could go through it ourselves.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What should we do...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: We've tried repeatedly to negotiate with Svarog, but he rejects every effort. He believes that Wildfire is a threat. Still, if it were you guys...
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Hmm... It's difficult to say.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: ...We have time. Let's get into the detail tomorrow. It's late, and you must've been through a lot. Go back to the town and rest. I'll make arrangements.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Again? I'm starting to get nervous of "arranged rest" on this planet...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: As for our Silvermane girl here... do you have time? I'd like to talk with you in private.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: It's completely blocked by the mine cart... What do we do? Can we blow it up?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Easy! It belongs to the mining team. We can't just destroy it. We should try and fix it.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Easier said than done... Do you know how?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah, of course, every Underworlder worth their salt knows how to fix a mine cart. Let me see...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Hmm. Even the pin connecting the body to the chassis is broken, not to mention the rear wheelset bearing. This looks like the work of Svarog's minions.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: We need to find spare parts we can use nearby. Argh, we're wasting time...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... Friends, do you need to find something? Findie can help.
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: ...How come you just jumped out on your own, little fella? Isn't your module thingy broken?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... My brainwave scanner module is indeed broken. However, manual input for search is still operable.
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: Come on. Input the name of the object you are looking for. Findie can help.
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: Oh, well aren't you confident? Let me give it a try then.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Where's the input interface? Ah, found it...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Mine Cart Pin... Mine Cart Wheelset... Confirm... Just like that?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... Request is being processed...
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... Match successful... Initiating search for lost item: Mine Cart Pin...
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep! Item found. Please commence search according to the Home-Use Object Finder Safety Manual.
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: Whoa! Stop! Ah! Stop, stop, stop! There's a big evil hunk of metal right there!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That model... it's one of Svarog's lapdogs alright.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Don't be afraid, I've dealt with those robots before. Let's go!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: What kind of days are we living through...
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: What else do you know about Svarog?
Did you bring those vagrants into the mine?
You seem to be familiar with Wildfire.
That's all I have to ask.
Svarog? I don't know much. The underground is in turmoil, everyone's focused on their own issues. Who has time to get involved in someone else's affairs?
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: I heard the vagrants say Svarog was protecting their base near the Furnace Core. Tsk, and there I was thinking he was one of the good guys.
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: Huh? What are you trying to say — that it's my fault?
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: You misunderstand.
No need to get excited.
Forget it, I'm just tired, that's all.
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: Even if those vagrants have no home to return to, they still have their dignity. They won't accept charity forever.
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: They needed honest work to get them through this hardship. So, I let them join the mining team. Can anyone really say I did wrong?
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: You did right, but maybe that's how the problem started.
Maybe you could have handled it better.
The problem started with them leaving home and being dependent on charity... If you want something to blame, blame life in the Underworld.
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: *sigh* When it boils down to it, they only chose to form a clique because the other miners never truly accepted them... I should've seen it.
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: They're a reliable group. Trust me, if we didn't have them, this area would be packed with monsters already. Just like Rivet Town.
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: I'm about to take the mining team over to Dr. Natasha. Take care of yourselves.
rows.speaker: Antonia

rows.text: Ah, young {F#lady}{M#man}. This isn't the best place for a chat. Let's keep things brief.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: What's so great about Svarog?
What happened in the mine?
What do you want to say to Bronya?
I've nothing to ask.
Svarog? He's an artificially intelligent being from the Old World. He was here when the underground was first constructed. That's about all I know.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Now he guards the Furnace Core hub. Many vagrants have established bases in the vicinity, seeking Svarog's protection.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: You got the gist from Natasha, right? The miners and vagrants came to blows over the vein, then Svarog's subordinates pushed everyone back.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Just pushed them back?
So Svarog wasn't after the vein?
Well, perhaps their methods were lacking in finesse, but that's essentially what they did.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: If you want my take, he prevented another Underworld conflict, even if the execution was rough around the edges.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: His behavior says something about his thinking: "As long as everyone's been driven out, the conflict is over."
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: You saw for yourself — after he pushed everyone back, he disappeared. It was clear: He didn't have any interest in the vein itself.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Well, I heard that she's a Silvermane Guard that was sent to arrest you. I expected you to be less friendly around each other... Are you worried about her?
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: We're working together now.
Don't threaten her.
Very much so.
Oh, working together? Understood. Rest easy, I won't make things difficult for her.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: We haven't seen a Silvermane Guard down here for a long time now. I just wanna ask her a few questions, nothing more.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Hahahaha, you needn't worry! That Silvermane girl wouldn't be afraid of an old veteran anyway.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Really? I'm surprised. Still, you can rest easy, I won't make things difficult for her.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: It's getting late. You should go back to the town and get some rest.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Wildfire, the vagrants, Svarog... The changes in here are greater than I ever imagined. *sigh* What exactly did the Underworld go through after the Silvermane Guards left?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Sorry, did you have something you wanted to say to me?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: What do you think Oleg wants to talk about?
What do you think of this Boss Svarog?
You and Seele work well together.
That's all I have to ask.
I think I know what it will concern. Even if Oleg wasn't looking for me, I would've looked for him.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I'm certain that the residents of the underground will have a lot they need to vent about. And as a Silvermane Guard, I have a lot that I need to ascertain. Nothing more.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: According to Oleg, he's a robot that took part in the War of Defense over seven hundred years ago. He possesses a near-human intelligence, and rules over all the machinery in the underground...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: During {RUBY_B#War Against the Antimatter Legion}the war{RUBY_E#}, the Architects created astonishing mechanical soldiers, but the fight was so terrible that most were damaged or destroyed. The technology was lost.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...If what Oleg says is true, then Svarog is an Architect creation leftover from the Old Era.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: We do? I hadn't realized. I've received rigorous military training — coordinating with soldiers under any circumstances is easy for me...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You can say what you mean.
So it's really only the training?
I admit, Seele is talented. We... do work well together. But that's all there is to it.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Hey... Thanks for your concern. You should head back to the town, and... I'll do the same when Oleg and I are finished.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Oh, it's you... It looks like the conflict is over for now. Thank goodness, if the numbers of wounded had kept climbing, I don't know what we'd have done. If only he'd have been here...
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: ...Now's not the time for those thoughts. I need to focus on treating the injured.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Can I help you with anything?
And who is "he?"
Thank you, doctor.
You've done enough. Treating the injured is doctor's work.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: So if you're not hurt yourself, you should go back and get some rest. Relax, if I need your assistance, I won't hesitate to ask.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: ...Could you pretend like you didn't hear anything? Now's not the time.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: The same to you and your friends. You've just arrived and already helped resolve such a sizable conflict. I don't know how to thank you.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: You'd best get some rest back in town.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: You guys have some moves. If you need my help with anything, just shout.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: So you finally believe us?
We need your help.
Hmph, it'll take more than that. But you're not as bad as I took you for. You walk the talk.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Oh, I wanted to ask you — that Bronya girl... Is she really a Silvermane Guard?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Yes, she's their leader.
You don't think she's got the talent?
Huh, couldn't even give it a minute, could you?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I've been on my feet all day. I don't have the energy for more headaches right now. Let me catch my breath and I'll come find you tomorrow.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Oh? She heads up the force? Hm... Not bad.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: It's just... I thought that Silvermane Guards were all cold and unfeeling — they left the Underworld to perish. But she... doesn't give me that impression.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Anyway, I've got stuff to report to the chief. See you around.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: No, no, she's got skill alright, I can tell she's got training.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Don't come any closer! The road's blocked — stay where you are!
rows.speaker: Bullheaded Vagrant

rows.text: ...Whoa, easy! Why are you hiding in there? Don't you know what happened in the mine?
rows.speaker: Anxious Miner

rows.text: What's that got to do with us? Do you think we're the same as those thugs?
rows.speaker: Bullheaded Vagrant

rows.text: Is anyone with you injured? We have a doctor. She can care for your wounded!
rows.speaker: Anxious Miner

rows.text: Yeah right, and you can guarantee that no one there with you is out for blood? I don't believe it. Stay where you are!
rows.speaker: Bullheaded Vagrant

rows.text: *sigh* These guys...
rows.speaker: Anxious Miner

rows.text: How about this one?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let me have a look...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: No good, all the components here are rusted. Let's keep looking.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: What about this one?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmm...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: The wheels are completely broken, but the connecting component should be pretty much okay. Let's remove it.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: That's everything!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You were a big help, Findie!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... It was nothing. Interastral Peace Appliances, your most trustworthy companion.
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... Current search complete. *yawn* Entering sleep mode. Please recharge the Home-Use Object Finder.
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: ...We're pretty lucky, huh? Without Findie, it probably would've taken half the day to find these parts.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Well, not that long... But that little machine definitely made it a lot easier. Alright, let's go back and fix the mine cart.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Hmph, fleeing at the first sign of danger... that's all they're good for.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Huh? What's this... Did those guys leave it behind...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Wh—Whoa!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What the heck!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... Searching for potential user...
Beep, beep, beep... Voiceprint detected. Looking up corresponding identity information... Oh my, it's an alien.
Hey, it talks! And it knows that we aren't from this planet?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It doesn't seem to be technology from here. Look — it even has an Interastral Peace Corporation logo on it.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Perhaps it's an antiquity left behind by some past interstellar traveler.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... Your mom's an antiquity!
Beep, beep, beep... Whatever, whatever. So you aliens know about the Interastral Peace Corporation? That's great.
Beep, beep, beep... Self introduction: I am Richard, the Home-Use Object Finder. Model information: Version 0.63, Professional model, Annual Deluxe package. Nickname: "Findie."
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: A Home-Use Object Finder? Who knew the IPC made these kinds of products...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... My brainwave scanner module is damaged. Please send me to an Interastral Peace Appliances retail store near you for free repair within the warranty period of 232 years 84 days.
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... Alien, please take me to an Interastral Peace Appliances retail store to conduct repairs—
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: What!? This fella's already broken... What should we do, take it with us?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's take it. Maybe it could be of some use.
My inventory is already maxed out...
Beep, beep, beep... Yes, yes, yes. When you need to find something you can't see, just call upon Findie. That's me.
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: Ugh, you need to log out once in a while.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's take it with us. It doesn't take up much room. And if it really is broken, there are trashcans everywhere.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... Not a trashcan! Yes, yes, yes. When you need to find something you can't see, just call upon Findie. That's me.
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: Let me see... Yeah, we can make do with this part. This little machine isn't half bad.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... What's that? Is that a hint of respect for Findie?
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: How convenient! So next time Dan Heng gets lost, we can just use Findie to find him, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... Biological life form search is currently not supported. If you have any questions, please call Interastral Peace Appliances.
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: ...Well, it was a good idea. Let's look for the next part.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep... Initiating search for lost item: Mine Cart Wheelset...
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep! Item found. Please commence search according to the Home-Use Object Finder Safety Manual.
rows.speaker: Findie

rows.text: Hey, what's that commotion? It sounds like there's a big argument happening...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Let's get closer and take a look.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Seeing it up close... this vein's even more spectacular.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I doubt the underground will ever see it fully excavated...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Are you gonna do it yourself?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Why wouldn't I? You've gotta be self-reliant down here. Watch, you might learn something.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Beep, beep, beep! Potential target object detected. The current search has concluded, entering sleep mode...
Oh, you must be Oleg's guests? Welcome to the Goethe Grand Hotel.
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: Goethe...?
Grand Hotel...?
Yep, you've probably seen that stylish Goethe Hotel above ground, right?
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: Uhh, not the most pleasant memories of that place...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's the above-ground branch of the Grand Hotel. A few hundred years ago, one ancestor of the Goethe family was ambitious, and sought to build something big from nothin'.
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: He eventually realized his dream and opened a hotel branch in the most expensive area on the surface.
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: Hey, that's not very polite~
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hahaha, it's fine. You aren't the first guest to have that reaction.
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: A few hundred years ago, one ancestor of the Goethe family was ambitious, and sought to build something big from nothin'. Eventually, he actually did it.
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: Have you seen that stylish Goethe Hotel? Strictly speaking, it's a branch of this Grand Hotel.
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: ...People with big dreams have big determination.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oleg wants me to take good care of y'all. Here's the key, you'll be stayin' in our most spacious guest room.
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: What do you think, [Trailblazer]? Should we go ahead and call it a day, or walk around a bit more first?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm tired. Let's go back to the room to rest.
Let's go explore the town a bit more.
The bed isn't very soft, but this room feels more homey than the coldly-decorated Overworld hotel.
So tired... hope I can get a good night's sleep.
Let's explore a bit more.
If we hadn't happened to be passing by... were you really planning to go into the Fragmentum alone?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Of course. What's all the fuss about? I've done that loads of times.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: So reckless... According to the rules of the Silvermane Guards, any expedition into the Fragmentum must have a squad of at least four members, as well as a communications officer.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Exactly, a rule of the Silvermane Guards. Don't apply your rules to us.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: (That voice again... such a strange dream.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (May as well go for a walk if I can't sleep.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Thank you, [Trailblazer]. If we hadn't run into you two, Seele would've had to venture into the Fragmentum on her own.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: I know it's not her first rodeo, but the thought of her taking on those horrid monsters... I can't help but worry.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: You seem to care about her a lot.
I think she can handle it.
Well, she grew up before my eyes after all. I don't want anything bad to happen to her.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: I know, but she grew up before my eyes after all. I don't want anything bad to happen to her.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Seele has been like this since she was little — impulsive and eager to be the best. For people who don't know her, they might find her... difficult...
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: But you can trust her, even with your life. Stick around a bit longer and you'll see what I mean.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: The place you are going to is called Rivet Town. Follow the path through the mountains to the north for a bit and you'll arrive there.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Let me think... I'm almost out of metal plates and bandages used for immobilizing broken bones. There's a market in the center of Rivet Town. Residents left behind piles of materials there when they evacuated. Please look for some there...
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Oh! Also, rubbing alcohol. I kept a bunch at the orphanage, since the kids often got into tussles. I didn't bring it with me when I left... I hope it's still intact.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: ...Lastly, painkillers. There should be a bunch stored in the old lab. Hopefully they haven't been destroyed by monsters...
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: These should be enough to get by for a bit longer. Be careful. Don't push yourselves too hard.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Metal plates and bandages, rubbing alcohol, and painkillers... Got it, piece of cake.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Let's go, if we leave now we can still make it back before sundown. When it comes to helping injured people groaning in pain, the sooner the better.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I can't remember the last time I went for a walk like this. I never thought I'd take one through such a strange place, with someone I'd only just gotten to know.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: It's so quiet here I'm not used to it... *sigh* The quieter things are around you, the louder they are in your head.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I'm surprised the vagrants in the Great Mine go after the mining teams, they must be desperate.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Still, whatever their situation, a crime is a crime. *sigh* How is the law supposed to find a balance between justice and compassion in the face of such complexity...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...How much longer can you last with your current supplies?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Is that... Seele?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: [Trailblazer], let's go take a look.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: But if you ask for my opinion, it's better to be safe than sorry.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I'll keep watch.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Actually, seeing as there's no one around... can I ask you some things?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You know, it was difficult for me to believe you. Some of the words you use are too alien for those that have lived their entire life in Belobog.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: In the past, Overworld soldiers on the front line would lose their lives in droves, and yet the Fragmentum's advance would remain unaffected.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The more I think about it, the more disoriented I get, which in turn makes me think about it even more... I just want a better life for the people of Belobog...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Maybe you're right, or not. Right now I just... need more time to think.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Aren't you supposed to be sleeping? What are you doing out here?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Here's the situation: The clinic is packed full of people injured in the mines incident. Since you helped us resolve things, Seele and I have been busy caring for them.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: As the Fragmentum spreads underground, more monsters go roaming around causing trouble for all the towns. That means more vagrants in the mines.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: You want to come as well? But you look quite tired.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Time to rest again. I hope there aren't any surprises this time.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That Oleg... he seems sincere. What do you guys think?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't you have something cool to say, like "Appearances can be deceiving"?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I don't try to disagree.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: *sigh* Happy now? [Trailblazer] is even starting to sound like you.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It has nothing to do with me.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Would you look at [Trailblazer], blurting out something so irresponsible.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: A lot like you, actually.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Fine, we'll keep our guards up. Our last hotel experience was eventful, to say the least.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: One of us should keep watch tonight.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: K—Keep watch? Are we space cowboys now? I guess this is the cosmic wild west.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hehe... *pretend yawn* Anyone else sleepy...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: N—No I don't! *pretend yawn* Besides, I've never pulled an all-nighter before! Do you know how bad it is for your skin?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Sure. I don't have much need for sleep.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You seem pretty exhausted, don't overexert yourself. I'll do it.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Bronya, did you finish talking to Oleg? Hope he didn't make things difficult for you.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Not really, though it wasn't the friendliest conversation. We didn't see eye to eye on everything.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I've come to know a great deal in a short time — I doubt I'll be able to fall asleep tonight.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I doubt I'll be able to sleep either... not that I don't trust you! It's just... you're a Silvermane Guard officer in the underground. There might be people looking to harm you.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I wouldn't be surprised if there are... the Silvermane Guards have a lot to make amends for down here.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: If someone had made a stand in the outset... and explained the consequences to Madam Cocolia... Forget it. It's meaningless to talk about it now.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You don't need to worry about me. Oleg guaranteed that I wouldn't be harmed. He seemed like a man of his word. Go and rest.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...I know. I'll go to Rivet Town and bring them back for you.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: It's too dangerous to go alone. Get Oleg to send someone with you.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: The rest of Wildfire has barely gotten any sleep the last few days. They should rest. They'd only be holding their eyelids open and slowing me down.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Besides, didn't you say some of the miners were gravely injured? Lives are on the line...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Up to no good, perhaps?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: We're just having a walk. Neither of us could sleep. You can rescind your baseless accusations.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Hmph. Walk somewhere else, then...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Easy, Seele, maybe they can help.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Haha, I'm grateful.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Hey, come on now, Seele's got a sharp tongue but a soft heart. She didn't mean anything.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Haha, oh yeah? Well look at you swaggering in like the protagonist in your own story.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: As you know, the underground is lacking resources to begin with. Add on the sudden nature of the incident, and it's no surprise that the clinic is almost out of medical supplies. We need to acquire more... somehow.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: *sigh* The situation in other towns is even worse than ours.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: You don't know him at all yet, do you? You can't rely on people like Sampo when it's important.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: The towns' resources have been swallowed up by the Fragmentum. To get anything now, people have to risk their lives!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Easy now, Seele. Anger isn't good for one's health.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Seele and I actually aren't from here. We both come from an industrial town to the north. A few years ago, the Fragmentum began to seep into the town center.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: I used to manage an orphanage and clinic there, but after the Fragmentum corroded the area, I had no choice but to move here to Boulder Town. After all, I have to survive myself if I want to save more people.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Go to a corroded town to collect some useful resources? I'm in.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Hold up! I never said you could join us!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: People's lives are at stake. Why wouldn't you want another person to help? Besides, I have some experience with the Fragmentums. I'm sure I will be of use.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: *sigh* Well... just don't slow me down!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: —Seele's lack of outright rejection means she approves of you, hehe. With you all accompanying her, my mind will be more at ease.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Come. Let me give you a list of materials we need.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Who goes there? Show yourself!
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...It's you. Don't sneak up behind me next time. Lucky for you I wasn't armed.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: No sleep for you either, huh?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I understand. The more that weighs on your mind, the more your fears become dreamscapes.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I know what you mean. I don't like the feeling that I'm not in control. And now...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...You need someone to look after you.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: This {RUBY_B#Source of the Disaster}Stellaron{RUBY_E#} you speak of... if you were to find it, how sure are you that you could stop the Eternal Freeze?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Your confidence actually makes me even more worried... This isn't like helping a child make a snowball.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I see... Well, thank you for being sincere. In itself, it's a comfort to me.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Is he your leader? I feel he possesses a great stillness of mind in everything he does.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: As far as I was concerned, Madam Cocolia's order to arrest you sounded reasonable... but why didn't she issue it straight away?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: She must have realized something about you... Something I haven't yet been able to perceive for myself, and it bothers me...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: What must have transpired to cause her such a drastic change? ...Still, orders are orders. It's not for soldiers to question their superiors.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I don't need you to absolve me. The truth is, I didn't have every confidence that I was doing the right thing, but the sense of duty to carry out an order is bound to prevail with me.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I don't need you to remind me, and I didn't have every confidence that I was doing the right thing. But the sense of duty to carry out an order is bound to prevail with me.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Nevertheless, that was her reason for deploying all the Silvermane Guards to the front line. The transport line for supplies and Geomarrow remained open, but the passage between the surface and the underground ceased. I approved of that decision...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I never thought that the Underworld would sink into such ruin without the Silvermane Guards... Perhaps mother was wrong...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: But how can I change her mind? I've tried, but she won't listen. I don't know how to get through to her...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Help me change the mind of the Madam Guardian? Not easy. Nobody knows that better than I do.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You mean...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...What was I thinking!? No... I shouldn't... That was a diabolical thought!
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Walk with me. Let's forget our problems for a while.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: We're here. This is Rivet Town... *sigh* Everything looks familiar...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Let's go, and watch your step. I haven't been here in a long time. There are probably some monsters around.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: We can't see anything here... Let's find higher ground to get a better view.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: This is the street alright. The orphanage should be at the end.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: These shops and signs... Why do I feel like I've seen them before?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: But when...?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The entrance to the orphanage is up this way.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I wonder what the old place is like now. Maybe some things will still look familiar.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: These stairs... they seem to have become more narrow.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Almost there! I didn't expect this place to be so well preserved.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Y'know, if we could've worked together to push back the Fragmentum... maybe we wouldn't have had to take off and leave our homes behind.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: There's a bunch of crates piled over there. Maybe we can find what we're looking for.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Watch out for monsters. They like to hide. If you need to, clear the area before you dig for the supplies.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: (What's that sound...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Oh! It's here, we found it! Thank you, Perkins!
Beep — Don't mention it, Clara.
Careful! Enemies ahead.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: These aren't like vagrants. They won't—
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Don't treat me like a new recruit. I'm all too familiar with the monsters of the Fragmentum. Let's get ready to fight!
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: A... restaurant?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Heh, the most famous restaurant in town. Natasha would bring the kids who behaved well here for a special meal.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: So did she ever bring you?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Do I seem like I was a goody two-shoes? Of course not.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: The facilities here seem to be in pretty good shape, not like those of a place that has been abandoned for years.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Now that you mention it, it does seem a little... Could people still be living here? Impossible...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...We made it! It's been so long... but this place hasn't changed one bit.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Oh! It looks like there's a lot of stuff piled outside. Let's go see if there's any rubbing alcohol for Nat.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Darn, how could they all be empty? Now even the monsters are gathering supplies?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: The monsters of the Fragmentum don't need any materials we humans use. And if they did take anything, this place would look much messier...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You mean that someone else got here and took everything before us?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: It's just a guess, but there are also some footprints on the ground here.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: *sniff* The scent of dirt is still fresh. They can't have come too long before us.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Let's go then. We need to find something, even if we have to search every corner of this market.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Why are you helping the vagrants look for medicine? If they're so great, how could they make a little girl go around running errands for them?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: N—No, it's not like that. I wasn't made to do anything... It's just that, the living conditions for the vagrants aren't great. There's not even a clinic in their camp. So, I wanted to help them out.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Also, not all of them are bad people... everyone just wants to survive.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Miss Seele, did this medicine belong to Miss Natasha? Then... can you give me some? The vagrants' injuries are quite serious.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: *sigh* I see. Let's split these painkillers then.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: R—Really? We don't need to ask Miss Natasha first?
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: If I know Nat, she won't mind. Although this will make it more difficult for us... she'll understand. She always does.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Great, thank you, Miss Seele...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Are you leaving? This old town is too dangerous. We'll accompany you part of the way.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I—It's fine, I have Perkins for company. And... I have some more things I need to look for here first.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Understood. Be careful, though.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Metal plates and bandages... rubbing alcohol... painkillers. Great, that's everything.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Let's go report to Natasha in Boulder Town, it won't take long to get back.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Ha... That was it?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Well, it was three against one.
It wouldn't have been so easy on your own though.
Nah, I could've taken it on by myself. But still... fighting alongside you two was pretty fun.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Please, you don't think I could do it? But still... fighting alongside you two was pretty fun.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Should be all clear now. Let's poke around.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: The kids at the orphanage were always getting into scraps when we played out here. If I remember it right, there ought to be some supplies for our cuts and bruises stored in that corner there.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I just hope the monster didn't get to them.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...It wasn't my imagination.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Huh? What are you talking about?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: This building, this playground equipment... I've seen it all before.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: What!? Come on, the overground and underground have been sealed off from each other for over ten years. It would've been news if a Silvermane Guard had come down here, let alone an Overworld princess.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Wait, unless, before that...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Yes, it's a possibility. That would explain why my memory of it is so blurry.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Come on, I need to look around a bit more before I can be sure...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: What's up here? Some kind of toy?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Yep. You pick, red or blue?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Hm... blue.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Ha! Look at this. After over ten years, the teeth marks are still here.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Teeth marks?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Alright, well... this one time, a big kid was trying to steal this toy from me. I couldn't outwrestle him for it, so I just bit down hard and hung on for dear life.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...How boorish.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: We've looked everywhere but here... I hope my memory is right.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: It's... Ah! Yes, we found it!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Great, and it's barely damaged! Nat wouldn't have expected her old supplies from years ago to have stayed in such good condition.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: You should still check the expiration date for things like rubbing alcohol. If it's expired, it won't be effective.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Hm, true. Let me check a few bottles.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Huh? What's this?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: This is...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Way over there, see that house on the hill? That's Natasha's old orphanage.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: After Oleg found me, he sent me there. I spent over half my childhood in that place.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: It looks quite impressive...
That must be a time of plenty.
I'd like to retire here.
Natasha said that the house was donated by some rich businessman. Whatever his business may have been, he must have been a good person.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Oh, I miss those carefree days as a kid...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: What? Nothing to say?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: No, it's just... this place seems familiar somehow. Never mind.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Weirdo.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Look down there. See the mess that remains of those old stalls? That's Rivet Town's market. The supplies Natasha wants are probably there.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Let's keep moving. Watch out for monsters.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...That object was pretty important to you, right?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Are you sure you're okay just giving it to Eric like that?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: If it will make him change his ways, it's more than worth it.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Hah, and what if he doesn't?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: From a young age, my mother taught me to be forgiving and to preserve the goodwill in people's hearts... Even if I am but a small glimmer of light in this world, I must try my best to shine brightly for others.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I must give him a chance, Seele, because other people can't.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I don't really get what you just said. Anyway, ahem, we should get moving.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Eric said that we need to take the shopping street to go any further. I think I still remember where it is... this way.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: (I should let those two be alone for a bit...)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (The only thing left to find is painkillers. I'll see if there's any nearby.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Uh... About that...
rows.speaker: Eric

rows.text: You're actually planning to give this little crook money? I'm telling you. This is his same old trick—
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I've only seen this kind of monster before in the restricted zone...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I—I used to live here... B—Before the Architects took me away, before Madam Cocolia adopted me... I used to live here! I'm... an undergrounder.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The Architects said that the guardian's successor is selected from among all people in Belobog. The selection process can take anywhere from a few years to a few decades.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Protect Clara. Initiating active defense mode—
rows.speaker: Guardbot

rows.text: Mm... Here you are. I hope the medicine is of help to you...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Mr. Svarog, he... he's my family. I met Mr. Svarog when I was real little. He took me in and took care of me.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Wildfire wants everyone to leave the underground... But Mr. Svarog wants everyone to stay here. According to his calculations, the overground is already unsafe.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: He says that his responsibility is "preservation." To do that, he must make decisions that best protect humanity.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: I know that Wildfire wants to talk to Mr. Svarog... But no matter how many times you talk to him, Mr. Svarog won't change his mind...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: ...Eric?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Hey, brat! How could you come here by yourself. Don't you know how dangerous this place is?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: S—Seele? Y—You aren't the boss of me! I—I can go wherever I want, it's none of your beeswax!
rows.speaker: Eric

rows.text: You took the materials and hid them all here? Not bad, kid.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: But if we didn't take care of those monsters, what were you planning to do? Just stay here, shaking in your boots?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Wh—Who asked you to do anything? I was just about to escape, I didn't need your help at all!
rows.speaker: Eric

rows.text: Still stubborn, huh? Then tell me, how exactly were you gonna get those big metal plates out of here past those monsters?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Um... There's always a way...
rows.speaker: Eric

rows.text: Don't let him fool you. Everyone in the Underworld knows that this brat is a no-good thief. If I remember correctly, even the clothes you're wearing came off another kid's back?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Don't be so polite to him. Everyone in the Underworld knows this brat is a no-good thief. If I remember correctly, even the clothes you're wearing came off another kid's back?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Tell us, what do you even want metal plates and gauze bandages for? We need them to save people.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: What?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Uh... 200 shield...
rows.speaker: Eric

rows.text: ...Are you kidding me? You want to negotiate?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Me neither... I never bring my coin purse with me on a mission.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: It's just 200... but I never bring my coin purse with me on a mission.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Not much, but I didn't bring my coin purse.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: No! ...Not this time. I really need money... my daddy...
rows.speaker: Eric

rows.text: Pretending to use your dad again as an excuse... If he knew about this, you'd be in big trouble.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Seele! That's enough.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: It's Eric, right? Here, you can have this.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: What... what's this?
rows.speaker: Eric

rows.text: This is a medal given to me by the Architects... See that blue stone in the middle? That's a Geomarrow crystal of the highest purity.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You need money for your family, right? Take this and show it to a knowledgeable buyer, and they'll instantly know how valuable it is.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: *sniffle* ...Th—Thank you! I...
rows.speaker: Eric

rows.text: But... you'll have to promise me one thing: You'll never steal other people's things again. Promise?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I—I promise! I'll never steal things again!
rows.speaker: Eric

rows.text: ...Then it's a deal. If you go back on your promise, I'm going to bring my Silvermane Guards with me and catch you myself! Here, take the medal and go back to the town. We already took care of any threat on the way. You'll be safe.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Th—Thank you, whoever you are! You guys can take all of these things!
rows.speaker: Eric

rows.text: Y—You guys need to be careful, too! There seems to be something real scary in that house up on the hill...
rows.speaker: Eric

rows.text: Oh, r—right! The road across from the market is blocked... If you wanna go further, you'll have to go to the shopping street.
rows.speaker: Eric

rows.text: Got it. Thanks for the tip.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: These crates have been sitting here for many years, right? Even if they have materials in them, are you sure they are still usable...?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Do you think undergrounders care about expiration dates? Even having any supplies is a miracle in itself.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: No... No... Empty...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: How are they all empty? Who could've—
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Careful! Enemy behind you!
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Hmph, I don't care how big you are. You dare sneak up on us from behind. This is it for you, pal!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: This is... something from when I was a child.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Wh—When you were a child!? Are you sure...?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: No, I remember now...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: There is no such coincidence in this world. I remember now...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Yes. I remember now...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You're... an undergrounder? Wait a minute... you're saying that Cocolia, the Supreme Guardian, adopted you? Then—
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Yes. I'm the successor chosen by the Architects. In the future, I will become the guardian who leads Belobog.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Why... Why didn't I remember this until now? My childhood memories are so blurry...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: No, mother would never do that to me... there's no way she would.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: During that time, all children of the appropriate age in both the Overworld and the Underworld will be tested. In the end, only one child deemed as "worthy" will be chosen.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I... must have been chosen from among the children here and then taken to the surface...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The kids at the orphanage are always coming and going... I never thought that there would've been a future Supreme Guardian among us! Does Nat know about this? Could she have been keeping it a secret...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...I don't think she knows. The selection of the successor is done with utmost secrecy, and the child chosen must completely say goodbye to their past.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.speaker: Irritable Robot

rows.text: Huh? Me again? It hurts, y'know!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.speaker: Malfunctioning Robot

rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Let me try and reset its system...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Certification system online. Please extend your right hand.
rows.speaker: Malfunctioning Robot

rows.text: *sigh* ...Why is it always me...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Aaaah!!! How come it hurt even more than the other two!? Hmph, at least that's the final step...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We can get in now, right? Hehe, Svarog's certification system is no match for us!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: This better work. Let's get back to the gate and give it a go.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Phew...That was scary, it just suddenly attacked!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Please extend your right hand.
rows.speaker: Certification Robot

rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Great, only two more steps to go. Let's move.

rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Sampo, what is this?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Ugh! Where did he run off to — he was just here a second ago!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It's that same type of robot again! Please don't tell me there's another round of "processing."
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Visitors for Svarog detected.
rows.speaker: Wandering Robot

rows.text: Protocol initiating... Scanning... Verifying.
rows.speaker: Wandering Robot

rows.text: Ooh, good plan! Treat the robots like guard dogs!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...How is that gonna improve our chances?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Are we gonna smash this one too? Count me in.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: She's his "family..." Did you really forget?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Family... Huh, weird.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't trouble yourself about it. We need to find her.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Obtaining audio data, please wait...
rows.speaker: Wandering Robot

rows.speaker: Wandering Robot

rows.speaker: Wandering Robot

rows.speaker: Wandering Robot

rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Wait, you guys went sightseeing in another town?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...It wasn't as fun as you think.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Indeed. And that little girl heading into the Fragmentum all by herself... It doesn't bear thinking about.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: That little girl heading into the Fragmentum all by herself... It doesn't bear thinking about.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Her strength belies her appearance, but even so...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You don't look so tough yourself. Well, let's find her. Svarog's not going anywhere.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Isn't this the robot that was following Clara around?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Shh, it's about to say something. Listen...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.speaker: Perkins

rows.text: Must... protect...
rows.speaker: Perkins

rows.text: In danger? What do you mean?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Workshop... target... must be eliminated...
rows.speaker: Perkins

rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.speaker: Seele

rows.speaker: Clara

rows.speaker: Seele

rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: You guys saved me — I'll tell Mr. Svarog about it.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: ...We were planning on paying him a visit.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Huh? What do you need to see him for? I can pass him a message...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: No, this time we need to set things straight with him face to face. Can you take us to meet him?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: But... Mr. Svarog doesn't like talking to others, especially Wildfire...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Don't I know it. But he's evaded communication with us for too long — this time we have to see him.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Um... I know you're working hard for the people down here, but Mr. Svarog doesn't trust human emotions. He only trusts his calculation results.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: So, I can't take you to see him... If Mr. Svarog and you had a fight, someone would get hurt for sure. Maybe even bystanders...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Listen kid, you—
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I know Mr. Svarog. He isn't affected by other people's wishes. He only follows logical judgments.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: According to his calculation results, the strength of the Underworlders won't be enough to prevent the disaster.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: His plan is to keep the Underworlders away from the source of the disaster, so they can survive for longer...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: ...Isn't that just putting us in a cage? It's ridiculous — what difference does it make if our death gets postponed a couple of days? How is that better than putting up a fight?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I'll definitely return the favor! But not like this...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: I'm sorry... I really can't help you with this.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: I'm always trying to convince Mr. Svarog. Please give me more time...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Um, if you don't mind... I still have important things to do. I'll go back now.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Clara—
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: It's no use, Seele. She's made up her mind. I could tell from her expression.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: We will have to think of another way...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Huh? Where'd she go? We just saw her go this way.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *sigh* We'll just have to head straight and keep looking.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hmm... why won't it...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Argh... I can't figure it out...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: ...Oh, it's you. You came with me after all.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: We couldn't give up that easily.
You're the underground's only hope.
You keep saying that, but...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Huh? How did you know?
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Yeah. I've fixed a lot of things before, but I never had to repair one as complicated as this.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Why isn't Svarog helping you?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I don't want to disturb him. This installation was... accidentally damaged by two of the vagrants. If Mr. Svarog finds out, they'll get in big trouble...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Was it really an accident...?
You give a lot of thought to others.
...Y'know Clara, if you're too kind, people can take advantage of you.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I think I found the source of the problem. You replaced the rollers, but the bearing is causing a jam — there's a misalignment.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: [Trailblazer], March, give me a hand. We should be able to fix it between us.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: More fixing? I'm getting good at this!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Uhh... If you can, please try not to upset Mr. Svarog...
rows.speaker: Clara

I have finished collating the Stellaron data and records. Do you wish to proceed, outsiders?

Requesting database materials cache. Serial number, 13175. Encryption level: Highest.

rows.text: ...This is the fruit of many years of research, Madam Guardian. The evidence is irrefutable: This so-called "Stellaron" is the source of all the destruction.
rows.speaker: Voice of Researcher

rows.text: The people will struggle to accept this conclusion, doctor. If we were to tell them that the almighty Alisa Rand activated this thing and triggered the Eternal Freeze...
rows.speaker: Old Guardian

rows.text: It's the truth, madam... The truth won't change with the opinions of the people. The reports before you are the precious result of painstaking effort on the part of Belobog's greatest scholars. You must trust the weight of its conclusion...
rows.speaker: Voice of Researcher

rows.text: ...I have never doubted you, doctor. On the contrary, I am resolute in the face of this conclusion.
rows.speaker: Old Guardian

rows.text: From the moment I took up this mantle, that voice... their voice — has made its home in my mind. I cannot shake them.
rows.speaker: Old Guardian

rows.text: ...I shouldn't be telling you this — let's return to your research, doctor. I'm afraid I cannot make these reports known to the public. Unless...
rows.speaker: Old Guardian

rows.text: Unless? Unless what? Please proceed, madam...
rows.speaker: Voice of Researcher

rows.text: ...Unless you have found a way to completely destroy the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Voice of Guardian

rows.text: I understand. In the name of Preservation... I will fulfill this mission.
rows.speaker: Voice of Researcher

rows.text: Cache number 13175, transmission complete. Next transmission: Cache number 24830.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: ...I don't understand, doctor. Why do we have to hide such valuable research results away? They're the work of a lifetime...
rows.speaker: Young Researcher

rows.text: *coughing* Y—You're still young, child. There will come a day... a day when you do understand.
rows.speaker: Old Researcher

rows.text: The Supreme Guardian... sh—she sees further than you or I. All her decisions are for the security of Belobog...
rows.speaker: Old Researcher

rows.text: I just think... it's a shame. Our research has hit an obstacle. Meanwhile, your results will be buried in the snow...
rows.speaker: Young Researcher

rows.text: *coughing* Don't be upset, child. You still have lots of time ahead of you. When you find a way to destroy — *coughing* — destroy the Stellaron... our efforts will have been worth it.

rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: You have arrived on Clara's recommendation. I will give you an opportunity to speak.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Hey, sounds like he's willing to communicate! Quick, [Trailblazer], time to smooth-talk him!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You seek peace, understood. Nevertheless, your statement is unilateral.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: My position will be determined after assessing the result of our negotiation.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: An inadequate pretext. You are not from the underground. You have no right to represent Underworld humanity.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Said question lacks the necessary context to be answered.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Proceed with your central point. Do not waste this world's valuable time.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: He cut you off completely! This guy...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Stay focused. Remember, we have to make him see that we're a variable in the calculation.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Think before opening your mouth!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Stellaron...
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Searching database... Access denied. Discussing "Stellaron" with unauthorized targets: Prohibited.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: You are broaching a secret that lies at the heart of this world. A secret that should remain unknown to humanity.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Reassessing targets... Threat index raised. I demand that you reveal your true intention.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: As expected... He knows of the Stellaron, but it's a restricted topic...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: We've come this far. Out with it already! [Trailblazer], just be straight with him! Everything depends on it.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Historical records state that humanity has already made multiple efforts to engage with the Stellaron. Without exception, these efforts have been motivated by human greed — attempts to secure the article for a selfish end.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: As instructed by the Architects: Any attempt to engage with the Stellaron will result in grave consequences. Reassessing... Target threat index critical.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: What should we do? This is going from bad to worse!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: There is no evidence to suggest you are an exception. Calculation result remains unchanged.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Target hostility significantly exceeds base index. Calculation result remains unchanged.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Peacekeeping protocol temporarily disengaged... Requesting extermination protocol launch.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: E—Extermination? In the literal sense?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Peace talks are over — March, prepare for combat!
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Mr. Svarog! Please, don't—
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Leave, Clara!
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Clara, it's dangerous here! Find somewhere to hide!
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Tsk... looks like we have to take action after all.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Prototype number 3, monitoring automaton Svarog, extermination protocol launch: Successful.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: ...Annihilation permitted!
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Hah, how can you put up your best fight without a doctor on the battlefield?
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: All of you, stay focused. I'm right behind you.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Nat? How did you...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Guess you guys had a bad talk, huh? Luckily, Sampo's got your back!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Base breached. Armed Wildfire personnel detected. Assessing...

rows.text: All subjects are high-risk individuals. Commencing complete annihilation!
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Beep... Boop...
rows.speaker: Irritable Robot

rows.text: Protocol... initiating. Scanning... Ugh. I'm so sick of repeating this.
rows.speaker: Irritable Robot

rows.text: Ha? What did this bucket of bolts just say?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Seems like this one's got a temper...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ugh, let's get this over with. Did you get your first certification? If not then you're wasting your time.
rows.speaker: Irritable Robot

rows.text: You mean this? Here, look.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Beep... Boop...
