rows.text: Whatever the case, we'll need it to identify our certifications.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: There's something wrong with this one...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: That's no ordinary kid. So young and yet so... stubborn? No, intelligent?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: She's incisive, and determined... in sharp contrast to you, March.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Did you really have to add that last part!?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It looks like we'll have to get past Clara if we want to speak to Svarog.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: If we can't even persuade Clara...
Is there any other way?
...Then good luck persuading that mass of metal.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: If we circumvent Clara and the gate, Svarog will only identify us as intruders. He'll be even more likely to give us the cold shoulder.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Isn't a robot shoulder cold to begin with?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Clara mentioned Svarog's "calculation results" many times...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: The strength of the Underworlders won't be enough to prevent the disaster... Those were her exact words. For me, that's our starting point.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: So... you think Svarog's logic has a hole in it?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: No, his calculation is correct. At its current strength, it is highly unlikely that Wildfire would be able to resolve the problems stemming from the Stellaron. However, that calculation didn't take the present situation into account. There's a new variable yet to be added to the equation...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: We're the new variable.
We need him to recognize our value.
...Precisely. If we can make Svarog believe in us, we can almost certainly overturn the result of his calculation, and we'll be one step closer to peace talks.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: But, how we can get him to do that... Showing him some of our photos wouldn't cut it, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: There's always a way. But first, we have to convince Clara.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I assume she must be on her way back to the robot settlement. Let's catch up with her.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Launching stage one processing. Please listen to the following question...
rows.speaker: Certification Robot

rows.text: Who is the reigning champion of the Internal Combustion Engine Rap Tournament?
rows.speaker: Certification Robot

rows.text: Dr. Dig
88 Degrees Bedrock
Relic Gang
Let's listen in on some conversations...
Correct answer.
rows.speaker: Certification Robot

rows.text: Certification result: Success. Requisite certifications remaining: Two.
rows.speaker: Certification Robot

rows.text: Please extend your right hand.
rows.speaker: Certification Robot

rows.text: My right hand? Here you go. Why is this part of the— Hey, hey! Ow, ow, ow!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...So this is the certification mark?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Great, only two more steps to go. Let's move.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Incorrect answer. Certification result: Failure.
rows.speaker: Certification Robot

rows.text: ...Uh, y'know friends, if you don't know the answer, you don't have to pretend you do. No one's gonna laugh at you.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Reassessing... Subject threat index: High. Initializing combat module. Threat elimination activated.
rows.speaker: Certification Robot

rows.text: Combat module? This thing's faulty, right...?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Wishful thinking, it's about to attack!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: This is Svarog's lair? I thought it'd be cold and lifeless, turns out it's pretty busy!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Many vagrants are staying here temporarily. Their homes were overrun by monsters.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Isn't it dangerous for them to make camp right under Svarog's metal nose?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: No. Svarog may be ruthless, but he never attacks without reason. For those with no home, this is actually a safe place to be.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Hm... If I hadn't moved away when I did, I'd probably be where they are right now.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Can we really fix this?
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Relax, we got this. Right, Dan Heng?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Less asking, more helping.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...I'm back, Timmy.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Welcome back, Miss Clara.
rows.speaker: Wandering Robot

rows.text: Timmy, open the gate please. I want to see Mr. Svarog.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Outsiders detected. Do you wish to permit access?
rows.speaker: Wandering Robot

rows.text: It's okay. They're all my guests.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Command received. Access restriction terminal unlocked.
rows.speaker: Wandering Robot

rows.text: Welcome back, Miss Clara and guests.
rows.speaker: Wandering Robot

rows.text: ...Wait, have mercy! I'm sorry! One certification, coming right up!
rows.speaker: Irritable Robot

rows.text: Hehe, now we're talkin'!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Okay, please extend your right hand...
rows.speaker: Irritable Robot

rows.text: (Put hand out)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: March, put your hand out.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Not you, the girl over there!
rows.speaker: Irritable Robot

rows.text: Huh? Me again? It hurts, y'know!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Ah! Owwww!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: There you are, only one more to go. Now, please leave me in peace...
rows.speaker: Irritable Robot

rows.text: Huh? Me again? It hurts, y'know!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Opennnn sesame~!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: See? Not so bad having Sampo on the team after all, right? Chief Oleg knew all along that I—
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Yeah, yeah, thank you very much.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'll commend you to the chief. No need to waste your time.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Alright, well let me issue a warning now: Everything from here on out is uncharted territory — we must proceed with the utmost caution...
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Now to set the record straight with Svarog. Let's get in there!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Ugh! Did anyone hear what I just said?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: C—Clara? ...You...
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Mr. Svarog can't fight anymore! Please... Please don't hurt him!
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Cla...ra...
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Mr. Svarog... Don't push yourself any further. Can you tell them what you know?
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Mr. Svarog, you said you were willing to make all my wishes come true, right? My biggest wish right now is for everyone to work together. Like... like family.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Recently, I learned something new... Calculation results can't always bring people happiness.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Even if the world outside the cage isn't beautiful... people still want to know what it's like.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Assessment system reset... successful. Processing variables...
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Variable 1: Clara's request... Variable 2: Outsiders' intentions.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: ...Updated assessment result: Transference of decision-making authority to outsiders. Outsiders are granted access to Stellaron intelligence.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: So... So we did it?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Clara seems like the only one who can break through Svarog's cold logic. It's a good thing she was here.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Yeah! Without her, even if we'd defeated Svarog, there's no way he'd have given us access to the intel, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Although, if Clara hadn't been here... Svarog would never have granted us access to the intel, right? Even up until the end.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I hope his memory bank really does contain data on the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Is this it, Nat? Us, Wildfire, the Underworld... Did... did we win?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: No, Seele.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Our battle... their battle... it's just beginning.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Finally... We finally made it to this point.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...What's up, nervous?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: No, but... I do have an aching feeling in my chest.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...I'm ready, [Trailblazer]. Reveal the truth. I'm listening.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: The Furnace Core... The path to the surface is close at hand now.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Thank you, [Trailblazer]. What you've done has brought new hope to the Underworld. Now we have to wait and see... But maybe this will lead to a new lease on life.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Your support came at the right moment. Thank you.
When did doctors start carrying weapons around?
Well, you should really be thanking Sampo. If it weren't for his intel, we wouldn't have made it in time.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: ...I, um... I haven't been truthful with you...
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: As Wildfire's leader, I couldn't simply look on while you fought on our behalf. We had to come help.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Huh...? Huh!? So, you're the real chief? Wh—What about Oleg?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oleg has always acted on my behalf — he helps me deal with all manner of problems in the Underworld.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Thanks to him, I'm able to make time for the people. I do my best to make sure that they have everything they need... At the same time, I was formulating a plan to deal with Svarog.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Your arrival unraveled that carefully crafted yet rudimentary plan, hehe... and for that, you have my utmost thanks.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: You're welcome, all in a day's work for a hero.
We did it for us, it wasn't as selfless as you made out.
Any chance of a more... tangible show of thanks?
When the Underworld recovers its freedom, the people will indeed extol you as heroes.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: A person is defined by their actions alone... I think that's how the saying goes? If the Underworld recovers its freedom, the people will see you as heroes.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: You have Wildfire's full support.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: However, even though Svarog is no longer sealing off the Furnace Core, there's no way that we undergrounders could go pouring onto the surface.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: That cold-blooded supreme guardian has used lies and tricks to keep the surface separated from the underground. If she detects any change in the Underworld, I don't know what she might resort to...
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: As for Wildfire, we need more time to build up our strength.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: With things as they are, you want to take a back seat?
It will be difficult for us to defeat the guardian alone.
No, but we need to wait for the opportune moment. In the meantime, I'm sending someone I trust to go with you.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Of course, there's no doubt about that. So, I'll be sending someone I trust to go with you.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Seele...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Didn't she tell you? In private, she insisted on accompanying you.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Don't let her carefree nature fool you — she's actually very discerning, and can read a situation like no one else.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Seele is a talented scout and a quick thinker — she takes decisive action. She'll definitely be able to help you. Not to mention... you also have Bronya now.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Will she stand with us...?
She got a big shock.
It seems like the intel we got from Svarog caused her a significant shock... but with Seele by her side, I know she'll recover.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: [Trailblazer], when's the last time you got some rest? I heard that you've been on your feet looking for Svarog since Rivet Town.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Health is everything — you won't be much use if you neglect yours. Let Wildfire take care of the Furnace Core for now. You head back and recuperate.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: If you're lucky... perhaps tomorrow you can return to the Overworld.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: You're right, but with Seele by her side, I know she'll recover.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Did you hear? Those idiots got into a fight in the mine, haha! It only got settled after Boss Svarog showed up.
rows.speaker: Devoted Vagrant

rows.text: I've said it before — only Boss Svarog can protect us down here. Everyone should follow his lead.
rows.speaker: Devoted Vagrant

rows.text: Well, what do you think? Cat got your tongue?
rows.speaker: Devoted Vagrant

rows.text: ...Do you ever talk about anything else? I'm so tired of hearing about Svarog.
rows.speaker: Reticent Vagrant

rows.text: B—But it's true. What else is there to say? Take a look at all these good-for-nothings... They'd starve to death without him.
rows.speaker: Devoted Vagrant

rows.text: Did you see those extra boxes of medical supplies at the depot? Who brought those over?
rows.speaker: Vagrant Newcomer

rows.text: Clara, I assume? I can't think of anyone else that'd do something that generous.
rows.speaker: Experienced Vagrant

rows.text: Who's Clara? Is she one of us?
rows.speaker: Vagrant Newcomer

rows.text: Not even close! She's Svarog's trusted family.
rows.speaker: Experienced Vagrant

rows.text: Family... of a robot?
rows.speaker: Vagrant Newcomer

rows.text: Well, you'll understand when you've been here a while longer.
rows.speaker: Experienced Vagrant

rows.text: Hold still. You're nearly fixed.
rows.speaker: Repairs-Duty Vagrant

rows.text: My design has been superceded by newer models. My components are no longer valuable.
rows.speaker: Grouchy Robot

rows.text: Hey! What are you talking about? I'm not interested in selling your components.
rows.speaker: Repairs-Duty Vagrant

rows.text: Take a good rest while you still can, [Trailblazer]. Your adventures on the surface won't be easy-going.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: So you're the leader of Wildfire.
Your "gentle doctor" act is pretty good!
What's Wildfire's plan?
What about Clara and Svarog?
I don't have any more questions.
Don't be surprised. My job is just to help everyone make the right calls.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: You remember Rivet Town? When the Fragmentum corrosion first appeared, we were defenseless. We didn't have a clue how to protect our homes.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: After we fled to Boulder Town, I made up my mind: A tragedy like that could never be allowed to happen again. That's why I gathered Oleg and the others together, and created the first sparks of Wildfire.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Afterwards, Wildfire began to grow. To be honest, I never thought a day like this would come.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: What do you mean? That's me too, y'know. The "me" that my patients see, at least.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Our identities are like masks. When we switch between them, we change the way the world perceives us.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: But our hearts never change.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Well, we don't want to act in haste before the situation has stabilized. We need to wait for the right time.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Ten years of being sealed away has sapped the Underworld's vitality. Now that the Furnace Core is no longer blocked off, we need to prioritize the people and replenish our resources.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Wildfire has never been in this for its own gain. Everything we do is for the citizens of the Underworld. That passage is a means to an end, not the end itself.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: We'll leave them be... Svarog may have blocked off the Furnace Core, but he's provided shelter to the vagrants from the beginning. An admirable deed.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: There are many homeless people in the Underworld. If they had safety and security, they wouldn't have to struggle to survive.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Wildfire can provide that while Svarog is recovering.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Things have settled for now, you should rest while you can.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: At daybreak, the guardian shall be a glittering star, illuminating the people's path.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: At nightfall, the guardian shall be a flickering flame, comforting the people's soul.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: So many years... Have I been following lies this whole time?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Hey... maybe you should find someone to talk to...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Don't let it get you down — you can share your feelings with others y'know? Do you think keeping it all to yourself is doing you any good?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: You let that status of yours go to your head, huh? Afraid to show weakness? That's why you're keeping so much bottled up inside, right?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: This isn't the Overworld. We don't do envy and etiquette down here. Whatever's on your mind, you can say it.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...I just want to be clear in myself, first. These fragments of history, the teachings I studied... It's all muddled together in my mind... I just... I don't know what I should believe.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...No, you just have to be clear on what you should do.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: You've spent long enough living in lies, Bronya. This is your chance to break out of the cage.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: How's it going, partner? Is that feeling in your chest the thrill of victory or just the joy of making it out alive?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: I know, your heart is bursting with gratitude... but there's no need to thank me. We have what I'd like to call a "fiscal friendship." If the money's right, not a problem in sight!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: When did you call in for reinforcements?
You knew Natasha belonged to Wildfire...
You seem to enjoy muddying the waters.
Thank you, Sampo.
Ha, I knew that you'd get yourselves into trouble eventually, so I got Oleg to send relief in advance. Pretty sensible, right?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: I'm asking why you went behind our backs.
Nice work, you saved us.
My assignment was simply to take you to Svarog's lair. I got the payment and delivered the goods — I wasn't obligated to tell you about my dinner plans!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: But I threw in something extra regardless. I only did that because we're friends, or I would've charged extra.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Here's a slice of life experience for you: Resourceful businessmen never get into risky trading without a plan b... and a plan b for their plan b. Plan c, we call that.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: My pleasure! Friends should look out for each other. Good for business.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: ...The chief? Of course I knew. Wildfire are mostly made up of torch and pitchfork types. How could they function without her?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Not that I'm criticizing old Oleg! He's good at the heavy lifting. It's just that Wildfire needs a meticulous thinker lurking in the sha— Ahem! ...Working in the background, hehe.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Hey now, you've got me all wrong! I just enjoy watching people fight, that's all. Fierce words, fists flying... what's not to like?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Easy there, don't get mushy on me now. We professional types don't have time for "thank yous." It's business! Feelings don't come into it.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Hahaha~ you see? Gotcha! Hah, seriously though — Sampo will always be happy to assist you.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Mr. Svarog, are you okay? Let me repair your language module first...
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Assessing... Language module operating as normal. Thank you, Clara.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Did your memory module get damaged? Maybe I can fix that too.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Retrieving memory module...
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Architect machine era records: Intact. War of Defense combat data: Intact. Geomarrow Development Group era records: Intact...
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Record of Clara's crafting of miniature magnetic drill rigs: Intact. Record of Clara's explanation of human "sleeping in" behavior: Intact...
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: S—So, your memory module is okay?
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: I have made a backup of all records pertaining to you, Clara. Do not worry.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: ...Even the one about sleeping in?
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: There are multiple backups. I can recover them at any time.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: Mr. Svarog, can I delete some of them...?
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: I cannot grant this request. Records pertaining to you constitute important data, Clara. They must remain intact.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: They are memories of family.
rows.speaker: Svarog

rows.text: ...I understand.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: Mr. Svarog, I still want to help you check a few other modules... Turn around a little.
rows.speaker: Clara

rows.text: She turned that way, quick!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: (Ahh, that was a good sleep.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: (I should go meet up with March and Dan Heng.)
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: It doesn't matter anyway...
What ever happened to trust?
I'm not seeing the apology here!
And why do we need you?
Just tell us the path you used before!
Oleg, give us someone else!
She's not going to help us?
She also has her own plan.
She left without Sampo?
Ahhhh... Well, now that we're done with that whole situation in the Underworld, we can finally look for the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: *sigh* But thinking about it, I feel a bit bad about Clara... We promised her that our talks with Svarog would go peacefully...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Svarog attacked first.
Sorry, I wasn't able to persuade Svarog...
I forgot to be more diplomatic.
[Trailblazer], you tried your best to persuade him. It's my fault for not preparing better for such a situation in advance.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: You tried your best, don't blame yourself. I should've considered such a situation in advance. And it was Svarog who attacked first, we didn't have any other choice.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: That certainly isn't our area of strength.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: I didn't mean for you guys to start beating yourselves up over it!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Look on the bright side — things turned out alright, didn't they? Now everyone knows that the real problem here is the Stellaron, and they're willing to help us out.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: All in all, the mission is going super smoothly!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: But we still have a lot left to figure out. For instance...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...Where's the Stellaron?
...Why does Cocolia have it in for us?
...Who is this Sampo character!?
Exactly. We don't even have the Stellaron's coordinates and location.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Cocolia's sudden change in attitude is also very curious.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Exactly. There must be a reason for this sudden change in her attitude.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: And, we still don't have the coordinates and location of the Stellaron.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: ...That's not of foremost concern.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: What's important is that we still don't have the exact location and coordinates of the Stellaron. Nor have we figured out the reason behind Cocolia's sudden change in attitude.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: We still haven't put all of the pieces together...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Actually, I've been having some dreams...
Dreams?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Oh, I remember you mentioned something about strange dreams before...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Telling Dan Heng and March 7th about the voices you heard in your recent dreams...
...All three dreams were the same, with Cocolia and that other voice...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: It would be weird to call it a coincidence.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I'm wondering if these dreams aren't just random, if there is some meaning behind them... Maybe you're having them because...
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Because of... the Stellaron inside {F#her}{M#him}?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: That's my hunch, but I have no proof.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Well then that's as good as nothing for now... So, what should we do when we get back above ground? After all this talk, we're still back at square one...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: We solve a puzzle one piece at a time. Let's get some rest. We'll talk to Wildfire tomorrow and get to the bottom of this.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Also, there's still one more key character we haven't talked to yet. Her connection to Cocolia may be the key to cracking this mystery.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Over there, see that? That used to be the worst street in Rivet Town... and it's also where I grew up.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: My friends and I used to wander those streets thinking about where to find our next meal. That is, until Chief Oleg got me out and took me to the orphanage.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: There I learned to read and write from Natasha. At the age of 10, I started to patrol the mines with Oleg, occasionally getting into fights with the local thugs...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...That sounds nice.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Nice? You being sarcastic with me?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Oh! No, sorry. Life in the Underworld is difficult, I shouldn't be speaking about it so lightly.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: *sigh* You're always so serious... It really gets on people's nerves sometimes, you know?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Right... Uh, what I meant was... I kind of envy you, Seele.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: For as long as I can remember, my days have been an endless cycle of studying, etiquette lessons, and training.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Every day all I hear is "Remember who you are, Bronya," "This is against the Architects' Admonishments, Bronya," "Ladies shouldn't use such foul language, Bronya"...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Some may envy this kind of life, but I have felt... trapped. When every choice and every goal has already been made for you... You probably can't imagine how that feels.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...No, I can't... But more importantly, what kind of "foul language" were you using?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: In the name of the Architects, I shall stick this spear into your nostril!
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Hahaha, that's it? That's nothing. Looks like I'll have to teach you some Underworld slang before you go back.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: No, no, that won't be necessary.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: It'll be better than poking people's nostrils at least...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I never thought that I'd be here having a heart-to-heart with the future guardian. As a kid, I didn't meet many people who lived in the Overworld. I only heard stories from the grown-ups and figured you were all just a bunch of cold snobs.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I've heard from some Silvermane veterans that before the orders were made to seal off the Underworld from the Overworld, there was no difference between the two places. Everybody ate the same food, chatted about the same topics, celebrated the same festivals...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Even though times are different now, things like the joys and sorrows of life, the ties between people... These precious things must certainly still connect us all.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: If there is a way to bridge the gap between the two worlds, we can definitely go back to the time when you and I were not divided. When we could stand side by side against the Eternal Freeze and the Fragmentum.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I'm not like you. I don't have that many grand plans for the future. But... if that's the future you want, I'm willing to build this bridge with you.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Thank you, Seele. Your trust is very important to me.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Speaking of which, what are you going to do next? What Svarog revealed must've made quite an impact, huh...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Yes. I thought I was prepared for anything, but...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: As long as I am the guardian's successor, those truths will come out sooner or later. But why does my mother hide it from me, and why does she want me to hunt down the outsiders who know about the nature of the Stellaron... It just... it doesn't make sense.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: I've thought it over. There's only one thing I can do — go ask her directly.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: You... Hold on, you're not really going, are you? Alone? You can't, this plan is...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I've already thought it through, Seele. I am Madam Cocolia's daughter. That will never change.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Be it my duties as her heir, or a Silvermane Guard, I must face my problems head-on. Even if...
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Bronya...
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: This is for you, Seele. Please help me pass it on to the outsiders. If... If I'm unable to see you again... They'll know what to do.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: ...Okay, I understand. You've made up your mind, and there's nothing I can say that will change it. But remember this — if you run into trouble, I will come to save you, no matter what.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Then I'll be waiting for you.
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: So... did you come to this spot when you were a child?
rows.speaker: Bronya

rows.text: Of course. I just didn't appreciate how nice it was at the time.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Very nice.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Took you long enough sleepy head. We've been waiting all day!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I've noticed that our sleep routines don't match up. You either keep getting up in the middle of the night or snoozing away until the day is almost out. Unacceptable. You gotta work on your teamwork!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: [Trailblazer], did you have a dream again last night?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Not this time.
I dreamed that Hook and Pom-Pom got into a squabble.
I can't remember.
...So that's why you slept for so long.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: ...Huh, that's weird. I bet the conductor won, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh, that happens to me all the time. It feels like I had a dream, but I can't remember anything about it.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Well then, let's go find Wildfire to discuss our next move and see if they have any new discoveries.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Let's go! I can't wait to finally get back above ground!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh! Look who's here!
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: It's the bane of Svarog! The big hero of the Underworld — [Trailblazer]!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: And the other big heroes, Dan Heng and March 7th!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Were those lines rehearsed?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Where's Natasha? Is she here?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: She has a bunch of other things to attend to, so I hope you don't mind talking to this old man instead. I speak on behalf of Natasha.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: By the way, sorry for keeping that whole thing about her being the actual leader of Wildfire a secret. Hahaha...
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: I'm glad you don't mind. Natasha is always cautious, but she has no ill intent, as you surely have noticed.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Hahaha, my apologies. Natasha is always cautious, but she has no ill intent, as you must have noticed.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Oh, well. I might just be second in command, but I still have a lot of responsibility. I couldn't give Natasha up right when we first met, could I? I had no clue that you bunch would become big heroes of the Underworld.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: She told me to make sure you return to the Overworld safely. I gave it some thought, and I think the safest way is to ask this fella for help.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: I brought you down. I can take you back up! Free of charge, satisfaction guaranteed.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: ...There's no need to knock us out this time, right?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Of course not! This time we'll go back through the Furnace Core.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Well, for my sparkling companionship of course! ...I jest, I jest! The path has been blocked for over ten years, and very few know how to get through. That's where I come in.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: That would be... problematic, and dangerous. Trust me, we should go through the Furnace Core.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Please, don't be like that. We have so much history together, can't you have a little faith?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Enough chatter. Just be a good guide!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Hold on. What about Bronya?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Why isn't she here?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: She already went back. As you know, she has some things to settle with the Supreme Guardian.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: What? She just ditched us and went back? How could you let her...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It's not like that! She... just has many responsibilities to bear. I don't completely understand, I trust that she's trying to solve the problem.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Exactly, she has a lot of responsibilities. I don't completely understand, but I trust that she's trying to solve the problem.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Enough about Sampo! We need him for this trip, and we can still get rid of him after we reach the surface.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Miss Seele, I'm still here, you know...
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Oh right, Bronya told me to give you this.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: She left us a letter. Hmm... could this be one of those "open-in-case-of-emergency" letters? I've never gotten one of those before. Should we wait until we run into something dangerous?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Stop overthinking and just open it.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Brother and sister Landau...? I know the brother must refer to Gepard, but who could the sister be...
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Oh, Serval! So she's Gepard's older sister!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: How very astute of you.
I hope nothing happens to Bronya.
Maybe the "sister" refers to Gepard.
Blonde, tall, good-looking... *sigh* Those Landau genes sure are something else.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: She gave it some good thought, but whatever's going on in that supreme guardian's head... Even Bronya might have trouble understanding.
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Hey, stay on track!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Sampo, do you know the Landau siblings?
rows.speaker: Dan Heng

rows.text: Landau... Uhh yeah, we're old friends. I've mostly dealt with the younger brother in the past, but the sister... *shudder* She's much scarier. Today's supposed to be a day of celebration, so let's not talk about it right now.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: We can set out at any time. Just come find me when you're ready~
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Well my friends, are you ready to head out?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Let's go.
Hold on, I have a question.
There's still unfinished business here.
Wonderful! Remember to bring enough food and drink to refuel on the way. We have a lot of steps to climb!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: What's the matter? Got too attached to the underground? Go ahead, I'll be waiting here.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Ask away, my friend. I have all the answers you seek.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Tell me about Gepard Landau.
Tell me about Serval Landau.
Tell me about the Furnace Core.
Tell me about yourself.
I don't have any more questions.
What else is there to say? You know him as well as I do. He's an upstanding guy, as well as young, handsome, and charming in his lack of charm.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: But to be honest, I'm not very close to him. After all, he's an officer and I'm... the opposite.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Oh, she's quite extraordinary. The renowned rebellious Landau girl. She once had a bright future, but after getting on her leader's bad side, she lost her job. She ended up opening a workshop and playing underground music.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: I heard that her old man was furious, and that only a few younger siblings are still in contact with her.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: I used to go to her sometimes when I had any mechanical problems above ground. But for... various reasons, I don't visit her workshop much anymore.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: It's a passage connecting the Underworld and the Overworld, a big, stone, spiral stairway. Y'know, I don't understand the Architects' obsession with making these steps when there is such advanced technology available. Wouldn't an elevator have been better?
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: ...It's easier for you youngsters. For this old guy, the steps of the Furnace Core are a nightmare on the knees!
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: You haven't heard enough about me, huh? Alright, my name is Sampo Koski. I'm a businessman who stands up for justice in his free time. And no, I don't have it in for you.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: You're back! I've heard from Wildfire that you helped resolve that whole situation with Svarog. Amazing!
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: It must have been exhausting. Please, have some food and get a good night's rest.
rows.speaker: Gertie

rows.text: I suppose it would be good to get some sleep...
Actually, I still have a lot of energy.
Ah, young {F#lady}{M#lad}. I wanted to see you off, but you know how things are around here in the underground. Solve one problem and three more take its place.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Hm, something you wanted to ask?
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: About you and Natasha...
I heard you came from the Overworld.
What's next for Wildfire?
I don't have any more questions.
Natasha trusts me. In her eyes, an ex-military officer was more suited to be the leader of the organization than a doctor.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: But the most important thing a leader needs is a strong heart. An ability to unite everyone toward a common cause. In that respect, no one in the underground comes close to her.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: I was actually once an officer of the Silvermane Guards. After being discharged due to an injury, I followed my old lady here to the Underworld, where I planned to retire.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: But as things would have it, I ended up busier than ever.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Do you regret it?
Do you miss the old days in the Overworld?
There is nothing to regret! Life in the Underworld is hard, but people here are kind and everyone is close like one big family.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Do I miss it? If you're talking about the time with my comrades-in-arms, of course. But other than that, I don't really prefer it over life in the Underworld.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Wildfire has already made it through its darkest days. With Natasha's leadership, we have the confidence to lead the Underworlders to a brighter future.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: And much of that is thanks to all of you.
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: Fortunately, Svarog turned out to have some useful information for you. After all your hard work, I'd feel quite guilty if you left empty-handed. Hahaha!
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: While you still have a long journey ahead, I have no doubt our paths will cross again one day. Till we meet again, friends of Wildfire!
rows.speaker: Oleg

rows.text: You ready yet? If you want to keep wasting time, I'll just go on ahead by myself.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: What, still something you want to talk about? Alright, let's make it quick.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Did Bronya say anything to you?
Looking forward to this journey?
Have you said goodbye to everyone?
That's all for now.
Not much. We just chatted a bit.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Care to elaborate?
I can tell something's weighing on your mind...
...It really isn't worth going into.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I promised her that I would help her rebuild the connection between the Overworld and the Underworld, that's all.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: ...Is it that obvious?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: I made a promise to Bronya that if something were to happen to her, I'd rescue her myself.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Hmm... I didn't really give it much thought. But traveling with you bunch does always lead to unexpected surprises.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Hearty combat and exciting adventures... Not bad, I certainly don't hate it.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Of course... Heh, you didn't see the look on Joshua's face. He could barely hold back his tears.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Chief Oleg... He didn't say much, but I know he's not the kind to wear his heart on his sleeve.
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: It was my choice to go up, and Natasha supported my decision. Besides, you could use another person who can fight, right?
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Alright, then let's cut the chat and move out!
rows.speaker: Seele

rows.text: Take a good rest while you still can, [Trailblazer]. Your adventures on the surface won't be easy-going.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: So you're the leader of Wildfire.
Your "gentle doctor" act is pretty good!
What's Wildfire's plan?
What about Clara and Svarog?
I don't have any more questions.
Don't be surprised. My job is just to help everyone make the right calls.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: You remember Rivet Town? When the Fragmentum corrosion first appeared, we were defenseless. We didn't have a clue how to protect our homes.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: After we fled to Boulder Town, I made up my mind: A tragedy like that could never be allowed to happen again. That's why I gathered Oleg and the others together, and created the first sparks of Wildfire.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Afterwards, Wildfire began to grow. To be honest, I never thought a day like this would come.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: What do you mean? That's me too, y'know. The "me" that my patients see, at least.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Our identities are like masks. When we switch between them, we change the way the world perceives us.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: But our hearts never change.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Well, we don't want to act in haste before the situation has stabilized. We need to wait for the right time.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Ten years of being sealed away has sapped the Underworld's vitality. Now that the Furnace Core is no longer blocked off, we need to prioritize the people and replenish our resources.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Wildfire has never been in this for its own gain. Everything we do is for the citizens of the Underworld. That passage is a means to an end, not the end itself.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: We'll leave them be... Svarog may have blocked off the Furnace Core, but he's provided shelter to the vagrants from the beginning. An admirable deed.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: There are many homeless people in the Underworld. If they had safety and security, they wouldn't have to struggle to survive.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Wildfire can provide that while Svarog is recovering.
rows.speaker: Natasha

rows.text: Things have settled for now, you should rest while you can.
rows.speaker: Natasha
